summary: Live blog and recap of the Seahawks' 24-3 win over the Giants on Monday Night Football (Oct. 2, 2023) at MetLife Stadium in Week 4. Seattle's defense sacked Daniel Jones 11 times and forced three turnovers, including rookie Devon Witherspoon's 97-yard pick-six. The note also covers pregame injury news, team stats, and broadcast and streaming details.
one_line: Seahawks beat the Giants 24-3 on Monday Night Football behind 11 sacks of Daniel Jones and a Devon Witherspoon 97-yard pick-six.
key_facts: The Seahawks beat the Giants 24-3 on Monday Night Football on Oct. 2, 2023, ending Week 4 of the NFL season.
Seattle sacked Daniel Jones 11 times and forced three turnovers: a fumble and two interceptions; Seattle had entered the week with just five sacks on the season.
Rookie Devon Witherspoon returned an interception 97 yards for a touchdown to make it 21-3.
Seattle improved to 3-1, including 2-0 away from home; the Giants fell to 1-3 and have been outscored 64-3 in two primetime home losses.
The Giants' other primetime home loss was a 40-0 blowout in Week 1 on Sunday Night Football; Jones' career primetime record fell to 1-13 and 0-3 this season.
Geno Smith threw a touchdown to DK Metcalf as the first quarter expired; Kenneth Walker III scored on a one-yard run, his second touchdown of 2023.
Drew Lock replaced Geno Smith in the second quarter after Smith was evaluated for a knee injury, and Lock hit Noah Fant for a 51-yard completion; Smith returned in the second half.
Graham Gano kicked a 55-yard field goal for the Giants' only points; Jason Myers kicked a 34-yard field goal for Seattle after missing from 53.
Jamal Adams returned for Seattle for the first time since Week 1 of 2022 but left the game with a knee-to-helmet injury and was ruled out.
Saquon Barkley (high ankle sprain) was inactive for the Giants, as were Andrew Thomas and others; Seattle's inactives included Charles Cross.
Seattle had 281 total yards to the Giants' 248, but the Giants had 36:00 time of possession to Seattle's 24:00 and committed three turnovers to Seattle's zero.
Kickoff was at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J.; Joe Buck and Troy Aikman called it on ABC/ESPN, with the Manningcast on ESPN2.
